sentences.text:
2 19-10-2023 Heard Mr. Arvind Kumar Singh, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner and Mr.
Madhura Nand Jha, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State.

2. The petitioner is a doctor who apprehends his arrest in connection with Sherghati P.S. Case No.
550 of 2023, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 417, 420, 467, 468 and 471 / 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 15(2) and 15(3) of the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956.
3. The allegation against the petitioner is of running nursing home in illegal manner contrary to the provisions as prescribed under Sections 15(2) and 15(3) of the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956.

4. It is submitted on behalf of the petitioner that the Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.64798 of 2023(2) dt.19-10-2023 petitioner has neither any concern with the patholab and ultrasound nor he is owner of any nursing home.
It is submitted that the petitioner having a valid degree holder of MBBS and M.S. is a practicing doctor since 1990.

He further submits that the person who was apprehended during the course of raid conducted by a team on the behest of Civil Surgeon, Chief Medical Officer, Gaya, he disclosed the name of the petitioner as one of the doctor who used to come in the nursing home for the treatment.
That apart, there is no allegation constituting any offence.

sentences.text: 5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes the bail application and submits that the petitioner was found involve in running a nursing home contrary to the provisions of Indian Medical Council Act.

6. Regard being had to the submissions made on behalf of the parties and considering the nature of allegation and the fact that no case is made out under Section 15(2) and 15(3) of the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956, let the petitioner above named be released on bail, in the event of his arrest or surrender before the court below within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt/production of a copy of this order, upon furnishing bail bonds of Rs. 10,000/- (ten thousand) with two Patna High Court CR.

MISC. No.64798 of 2023(2) dt.19-10-2023 sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned A.C.J.M. - Ist, Sherghati (Gaya) in connection with Sherghati P.S. Case No. 550 of 2023, subject to the conditions laid down in Section 438(2) Cr.P.C. with the further condition that one of the bailors shall be the own/close family members of the petitioner.

(Harish Kumar, J) saurabhkr/-
